 Oral Judgment
Though the appeals are listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
2. A common judgment was passed on 29.01.2020 in MVC Nos.449/2019 and 450/2019 by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Kalaburagi (for short 'the Tribunal').
MFA No.200982/2021 is filed by the claimant in MVC No.450/2019 and MFA No.202827/2023 is filed by the claimant in MVC No.449/2019.

3. IN MFA No.200982/2021 (MVC No.450/2019):
The claimant, aged 45 years, doing tailoring, met with an accident on 11.04.2018 and sustained grievous injures.

Therefore, she filed a claim petition before the NC:
2025:KHC-K:7488 HC-KAR Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.14,50,000/-.

The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted compensation of Rs.3,13,900/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directed the respondent-Corporation to deposit the same.

4. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the injured claimant has preferred this appeal, in which it is contended that, she was doing tailoring and earning Rs.20,000/- per month, and filed Ex.P20-Tailor Training Certificate, but the Tribunal has not considered the same.

As per Ex.P14,
future medical expenses are not granted.
She was aged 45 years, but the multiplier has not rightly taken.
She examined the doctor as PW.3 and he assessed the disability at 35% to the whole body, but the Tribunal has taken only 12%.
Therefore, requested for enhancement of compensation.
5. Heard the arguments of both sides.

3 6.

Though the appellant produced Ex.P20 and stated that she was earning Rs.20,000/- per month,
she has not filed any income proof.
Therefore, the Tribunal has taken her income at Rs.9,000/- per month.
But, as the accident is of the year 2018, as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, her notional income is to be taken at Rs.11,750/- per month.

It was observed by the Tribunal that, in the petition her age is shown as 45 years but in the FIR and charge sheet, her age is shown as 50 years and therefore, the Tribunal considered her age as 50 years and taken the multiplier as '13', which needs no interference.
As per the discharge card - Ex.P13, the appellant was admitted in the hospital from 11.04.2018 to 17.04.2018 i.e., for 07 days.
The appellant examined the doctor as PW.3 and he assessed the disability under Ex.P15 at 35% to the whole body.
The Tribunal has taken 12% i.e., 1/3rd of 35%.

Learned counsel for the appellant contended that, it is to be taken atleast 20%, whereas, learned counsel for the respondent NC: 2025:KHC-K:7488 HC-KAR objected the same and stated that, the Tribunal has rightly considered the disability.

As per the disability certificate - Ex.P15, the appellant has sustained fracture of left tibia and fracture medial condyle and split fracture lateral condyle of left tibia was operated with MIPPO Buttress plaiting for medial condyle and CC screw for lateral condyle of tibia and she requires another surgery for removal of implant and the estimated cost is Rs.45,000/-.
As there is minimal malunited fracture of medial condyle left tibia with implant in situ with stiffness of left knee, the disability is assessed at 35% to the whole body.
The Tribunal has rightly considered 1/3rd of the same as 12%, which needs no interference.

Thus, the loss of future earnings would be:
Rs.11,750 x 12 x 13 x 12% = Rs.2,19,960/-.
7.
The Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.1,02,900/- towards medical expenses and it needs no interference.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7488 HC-KAR 8.
The appellant was admitted in the hospital for 07 days.

Considering the nature of injuries and period of hospitalisation, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.60,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.30,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
9. The appellant might not have attended any work at least for a period of four months due to the injuries sustained.

Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.47,000/-
(Rs.11,750 x 4) for loss of income during laid up period.
10. PW.3 stated that, the appellant requires another surgery for removal of implant and the estimated cost is Rs.45,000/-.
Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.30,000/- for future medical expenses i.e., for removal of implant.
11. Hence, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:

Medical expenses Rs.1,02,900/-

Thus, the appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.2,05,960/- with interest at 6% per annum.

12. IN MFA No.202827/2023 (MVC No.449/2019):
The claimant, aged 65 years, doing tailoring, met with an accident on 11.04.2018 and sustained grievous injures.

Therefore, she filed a claim petition before the Tribunal,
claiming compensation of Rs.14,50,000/-.

The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, granted compensation of Rs.1,52,500/- with interest at NC:
2025:KHC-K:7488 HC-KAR 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directed the respondent-Corporation to deposit the same.

13. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the injured claimant has preferred this appeal, in which it is contended that, she examined the doctor as PW.4 and he assessed the disability at 22.98% as per Ex.P21-disability certificate, but the Tribunal has taken only 7%.
As per Ex.P21, the doctor estimated the cost for future surgical expenses as Rs.2,50,000/-.
Therefore, requested for enhancement of compensation.

14. Heard the arguments of both sides.
15.
PW.4 is a dental surgeon.

He stated that, there is deviation in opening and closing of mandible,
tenderness in R1 and L1 TNS and facial aesthetic is affected, she cannot pronounce the words properly and cannot masticate any kind of food and thus, he assessed the disability at 22.98% under Ex.P21- disability certificate.

He also stated that, the appellant lost 8 teeth and she - 10 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7488 HC-KAR requires surgery for implanting the said teeth and the estimated cost is Rs.2,40,000/- and it may increase to Rs.2,50,200/-.
1/3rd of 23% comes to 8%.

Therefore,
this Court finds it reasonable to take the disability at 8%.
The Tribunal has considered the age of the appellant as 70 and the multiplier was rightly taken as '5'.

Therefore, as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, as the accident is of the year 2018, her notional income is to be taken at Rs.11,750/- per month.

Thus, the loss of future earnings would be:
Rs.11,750 x 12 x 5 x 8% = Rs.56,400/-.
16.
The appellant has produced medical bills under Ex.P10 and the Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.24,200/- towards medical expenses and it needs no interference.
The appellant was admitted in the hospital for 03 days.

Considering the nature of injuries and period of hospitalisation, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.50,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.25,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
18. The appellant might not have attended any work at least for a period of three months due to the injuries sustained.

Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.32,250/-
(Rs.11,750 x 3) for loss of income during laid up period.
19. PW.4-doctor stated that, the appellant has lost 8 teeth and she requires surgery and thereby estimated the cost of implanting the said teeth as Rs.2,40,000/-.
The Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.50,000/- towards future medical expenses.
This Court finds it reasonable to enhance the same to Rs.1,00,000/-.

Hence, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.24,200/-
Future medical expenses Rs.1,00,000/-
Loss of future earnings Rs.56,400/-
Loss of income during laid up period Rs.35,250/-
Transportation, extra nourishment, Rs.30,000/-
and attendant charges Loss of amenities Rs.25,000/-
Total Rs.3,20,850/-
Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.1,52,500/-
Enhancement: Rs.1,68,350/-

Thus, the appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,68,350/- with interest at 6% per annum.

21. In the result, the following order is passed:
(i) Both the appeals are allowed in part.

(ii) The appellant in MFA No.200982/2021 is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.2,05,960/-
with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
- 13 - NC: 2025:KHC-K:7488 HC-KAR (iii) The appellant in MFA No.202827/2023 is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.1,68,350/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
(iv) The respondent-Corporation is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount in both the appeals within one month from the date of this judgment.
(v) On such deposit, the appellants in both the appeals are permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
(vi) It is made clear that, as per the order dated 16.08.2023, the appellant in MFA No.202827/2023 is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 426 days in filing the appeal.
